Everything below was learned purely by running `/workspace/executable` in a PTY and
observing bytes. No tracing/disassembly was used.

Test JSON inputs:
- `/harness/tests/08/small.json` — `{"a": 1, "b": [true, false, null], "c": "hello"}` → frame 5 rows × 14 cols on an 80×24 terminal.
- `/harness/tests/08/tall.json` — `{"k1": [1..20], "k2": {"x": 1, "y": 2}, "k3": "z"}` → frame 8 rows × 14 cols (k1 initially collapsed, k2 expanded).
- `/harness/tests/08/wide.json` — `["aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", 1]` → frame 4 rows × 27 cols.
- `/harness/tests/03/root_scalar_num.json` — `42` → frame 1 row × 2 cols.

Captures: `/harness/captures/08/<scenario>/stepN.bin` (step0 = initial output, stepN =
output after Nth input token). Runner: `/harness/pty2.py`; my extended runner
`/harness/pty3.py` additionally auto-replies to terminal queries (DECRQSS/DSR) and
supports `SIGNAL:SIGxxx` step tokens.

The output is **fully deterministic**: identical runs produce byte-identical captures
(verified on repeated runs). The only input-dependent variation found is the exit
cursor-style sequence, which depends on the terminal's DECRQSS reply (see §6).

---

## 1. Startup sequence

Inline (default) mode, first bytes emitted (od of `base_small/step0.bin`, offsets 0–47):

```
00 1b 50 24 71 20 71 1b 5c 1b 5b 3f 37 6c 1b 5b  >..P$q q.\.[?7l.[<
3f 31 30 30 30 68 1b 5b 3f 31 30 30 33 68 1b 5b  >?1000h.[?1003h.[<
3f 31 30 31 35 68 1b 5b 3f 31 30 30 36 68 00     >?1015h.[?1006h.<
```

Exactly, in order:
1. `\x00` (a literal NUL byte)
2. `\x1bP$q q\x1b\\` — DECRQSS requesting current cursor style (DECSCUSR)
3. `\x1b[?7l` — wraparound OFF (stays off for the whole session)
4. `\x1b[?1000h` `\x1b[?1003h` `\x1b[?1015h` `\x1b[?1006h` — mouse: click tracking, any-motion tracking, UTF-8 ext, SGR ext (four separate sequences, this order)
5. `\x00` — second NUL
6. immediately followed by the first frame (see §2), which starts with `\r\x1b[2K`.

Fullscreen mode (`-f`/`--fullscreen`): same, except `\x1b[?1049h` (alternate screen)
is inserted directly after the DECRQSS and before `\x1b[?7l`:
`\x00` `\x1bP$q q\x1b\\` `\x1b[?1049h` `\x1b[?7l` mouse-on×4 `\x00`.

Reading JSON from a pipe (no file argument): stdout gets the literal text
`Reading from stdin...` (15 bytes, no newline) *before* the initial `\x00`; the rest of
startup is identical. The first frame's `\r\x1b[2K` erases that line.

No terminal-identification queries (DA, XTGETTCAP, etc.) are ever sent. The only
queries the app ever emits are the startup DECRQSS and the per-frame DSR (§4).

## 2. Frame structure

Every screen update ("frame") is one contiguous write burst with this grammar:

```
frame  = prefix  content  suffix
prefix = first-frame:  "\r\x1b[2K"
         later frames: undo  "\r"  up-moves  ["\x1b[J\x1b[H"]  ["\x1b[6n"]
undo   = ["\x1b[{D}B"] ["\x1b[{R}C"]      ; exact inverse of previous frame's suffix move
up-moves = plain mode:  "\x1b[1A" repeated (H_old - 1) times
           clear mode:  ("\x1b[2K\x1b[1A") repeated (H_old - 1) times, then "\x1b[2K"
content = H rows of cells, rows separated by "\r\r\n" (CR CR LF)
suffix = ["\x1b[{U}A"] ["\x1b[{L}D"]  "\x1b[?25l"  "\x00"
```

- `H_old` = number of rows of the *previous* frame, `H`/`W` = rows/cols of *this* frame.
- Cursor moves with value 0 are **omitted entirely** (never `\x1b[0A`). Negative values
  are emitted **literally** (see the `\x1b[-1A` quirk in §3).
- `\x1b[6n` (DSR) appears only in the 2nd and 3rd frames of the session (see §4).
- `\x1b[J\x1b[H` appears only when the frame got narrower (see §5).

Content rows: each row is written left-to-right with SGR sequences inline; rows are
padded with spaces to the frame width W **except** the last content row, which is
padded too (observed: last row also padded to W — e.g. `}             ` in
base_small). Rows are joined by `\r\r\n` (three bytes: CR CR LF). There is no
trailing `\r\r\n` after the last row; the suffix follows the last row's bytes directly.

Suffix (end-of-frame cursor placement): after writing the last row the cursor is at
(end row, col W+1). The app then moves it to the "focused cell" of the currently
selected element:

- `U = H - 1 - sel_row`  (`sel_row` = 0-based row of the selected element)
- `L = W + 1 - cursor_col`  (`cursor_col` = 1-based column of the **last** character
  of the selected/inverted token — verified for scalars (`1` → its own column),
  strings (closing `"`), and collapsed containers (`[...],` → the comma column);
  single-char tokens like `{` have first == last).

Then `\x1b[?25l` (hide cursor) and a trailing `\x00`.

The next frame's `undo` is the exact inverse: `\x1b[{U}B\x1b[{L}C` (same U and L
numbers, down/right instead of up/left), returning the cursor to (end row, col W+1)
of the previous frame. Then `\r` and the up-moves bring it to the frame's top-left.
Verified across many frames, e.g.:

```
frame ends   ...\x1b[4A\x1b[14D\x1b[?25l\x00      next frame starts \x1b[4B\x1b[14C\r...
frame ends   ...\x1b[3A\x1b[7D\x1b[?25l\x00       next frame starts \x1b[3B\x1b[7C\r...
```

Worked example (small.json, DOWN pressed; `base_small/step1.bin`):

```
1b 5b 34 42 1b 5b 31 34 43 0d                       \x1b[4B\x1b[14C\r      undo + CR
1b 5b 31 41 (×4)                                    \x1b[1A × (H_old-1)=4   plain up-moves
1b 5b 36 6e                                         \x1b[6n                 DSR (frame #2)
... 5 content rows joined by 0d 0d 0a ...
1b 5b 33 41 1b 5b 37 44 1b 5b 3f 32 35 6c 00        \x1b[3A\x1b[7D\x1b[?25l\x00
```

## 3. Edge cases of the suffix formula

- Selection can never be on the last content row in practice (closing-brace rows are
  not selectable and the viewport keeps a margin), so `U ≥ 1` normally.
- Root scalar document (`42`, H=1, W=2): the app places the "focused cell" one row
  *below* the single row, producing a **negative** parameter which is emitted
  literally (od of `root_scalar/step0.bin` tail):

  ```
  ...\x1b[7m\x1b[96m\x1b[49m42\x1b[27m\x1b[39m\x1b[49m\x1b[-1A\x1b[1D\x1b[?25l\x00
  ```
  and the next frame begins with the mirror image `\x1b[-1B\x1b[1C\r...`.
  Rule: compute `U = H-1-sel_row` as a signed integer; emit `\x1b[{U}A` iff `U != 0`,
  even if negative. Same for `L`, `undo`, and the exit cursor-restore.
- Zero case: collapsed root (`wide.json` after ENTER → 1-row frame `[...]`): the
  suffix is just `\x1b[1D\x1b[?25l\x00` (U=0 omitted) and the next frame prefix is

small.json (`sigint/step1.bin`):

```
\x1b[4B\x1b[14C \x1b[?1006l\x1b[?1015l\x1b[?1003l\x1b[?1000l \x1b[?7h \x1b[?25h \x1b[2 q \x00\r\r\n
```
(SIGTERM byte-identical; the `\x1b[2 q` here reflects the DECRQSS reply sent by pty3.)
Fullscreen + SIGINT: same, with `\x1b[?1049l` before `\x1b[?25h`, ending `\x00\r`
(`sigint_full/step1.bin`, 68 bytes).

### 6c. Ctrl-C as a *byte* (0x03) does NOT exit

The pty is in raw mode (ISIG off), so writing `0x03` to the master delivers a byte,
not a signal. The app treats it as an unknown key: full redraw, no exit. Same for
Ctrl-D (`0x04`). Only an actual SIGINT/SIGTERM signal exits. Exit codes: q, ESC,
SIGINT, SIGTERM all → exit code 0.

### 6d. SIGHUP, SIGKILL etc.

SIGHUP: process dies instantly with **zero** output — no cleanup at all
(`sighup/step1.bin` is empty). The terminal is left with mouse modes on etc.

## 7. Input parsing behavior (as observable from output)

- **One frame per input batch.** Every read() of input bytes that the event loop
  processes produces exactly one complete frame, even if nothing changed:
  - Unknown keys (`x`, digits, Ctrl-bytes like 0x03/0x04) → full redraw, identical
    bytes to a no-op (`noop_keys/step1.bin` == `step2.bin`).
  - A key that changes nothing (UP at top) → full redraw anyway, byte-identical to
    an unknown-key redraw.
  - Multiple keys in ONE write (`xx` as one token) → ONE frame
    (`batch_xx/step1.bin` = 246 bytes = same as a single `x`).
  - Two writes 10 ms apart → TWO frames. So coalescing is per-read, not time-based.
- **Lone ESC timeout ≈ 80 ms** (measured: no exit within an 80 ms window, exit
  within an 82 ms window; treat as ~80 ms, timing-sensitive at the boundary). An ESC
  byte is held waiting for a possible escape sequence; if nothing follows within the
  timeout it is delivered as the Escape key → exit. If `[A` follows within the
  timeout it is parsed as Up and no exit occurs (`esc_partial/`).
- A partial/unrecognized escape byte still triggers a redraw at the time it is
  received (the lone-ESC capture produced a full frame *before* the timeout fired).
- Terminal query replies (DSR `\x1b[{r};{c}R`, DECRQSS response) are consumed
  silently — no redraw, no output change (except DECRQSS → exit cursor style, §6a).
- **Key-table discrepancy (cross-check for the keybindings area):** the `-k` help
  says "top: gg / bottom: G", but observed behavior is the opposite: `gg` jumps to
  the **bottom** selectable row and `G` jumps to the **top** (verified on small.json
  and tall.json: `gg_tall/` row 0→6, `G_tall/` row 3→0). PGUP/PGDN behavior is also
  nontrivial (on tall.json from row 0: PGDN→1, PGDN→6, PGUP→1) — left to the
  navigation area.
- TAB moves selection down one row (like Down) and triggers a normal frame.
- Idle: with no input for 2 s the app emits nothing — no periodic/animation frames
  (`idle2s/step0.bin` byte-identical to the quick run).

## 8. Complete inventory of escape sequences ever emitted

Swept over all ~200 capture files in `/harness/captures/08/`. The app only ever emits:

- DCS: `\x1bP$q q\x1b\\` (DECRQSS cursor style, once at startup)
- CSI cursor moves: `\x1b[{n}A` `\x1b[{n}B` `\x1b[{n}C` `\x1b[{n}D` (n can be `-1`;
  `\x1b[1A` is always emitted singly/repeated, never combined into `\x1b[4A` in the
  up-moves; all other moves use a single sequence with the full count)
- `\x1b[2K` (erase line), `\x1b[J` (erase below), `\x1b[H` (home) — only in the
  clear/width-shrink cases of §5
- `\x1b[6n` (DSR, frames #2/#3 only)
- SGR: `\x1b[1m` `\x1b[22m` (bold on/off for containers), `\x1b[7m` `\x1b[27m`
  (inverse for selection), colors `\x1b[91m` `\x1b[92m` `\x1b[93m` `\x1b[94m`
  `\x1b[96m` always paired with `\x1b[49m` and closed by `\x1b[39m\x1b[49m`
- Modes: `\x1b[?7l`/`\x1b[?7h`, `\x1b[?25l`/`\x1b[?25h`, mouse `\x1b[?1000h/l`
  `\x1b[?1003h/l` `\x1b[?1015h/l` `\x1b[?1006h/l`, `\x1b[?1049h/l` (fullscreen only)
- `\x1b[{S} q` (DECSCUSR) only at exit

Never emitted: bell `\x07`, bracketed paste (`?2004`), focus events (`?1004`),
synchronized output (`?2026`), kitty/xtwinops queries, DA `\x1b[c`, DECRQM, or any
OSC. No `\x1b[2J` ever.

## 9. The `\x00` (NUL) bytes — complete inventory

NULs appear at exactly these positions and nowhere else (verified by scanning every
capture):

1. The very first byte of the session (before DECRQSS).
2. Immediately after the mouse-modes-on burst at startup (before the first frame).
3. At the end of **every** frame, right after `\x1b[?25l`.
4. In the exit burst, right after `\x1b[{S} q` (before the final `\r\r\n` / `\r`).

So: step0 captures contain 3 NULs (offsets 0, 46, and last byte for inline
small.json), plain frame captures contain 1 NUL (last byte), q/ESC exit captures
contain 2 NULs (end of final redraw + in the shutdown), SIGINT exits contain 1 NUL.

## 10. Timing/non-determinism notes for the reimplementation

- Output is byte-deterministic for a fixed input script (repeated runs compared
  equal). No timestamps, no randomness.
- Input coalescing is per-read(): bytes that arrive in one read produce one frame;
  bytes in separate reads produce one frame each. A byte-exact harness must therefore
  control write batching.
- The lone-ESC disambiguation timeout is ≈80 ms — scripts that send a bare ESC must
  wait longer than that (and scripts testing ESC sequences must send the bytes in one
  write or within the timeout).
- The DECRQSS/DSR replies must be delivered promptly after the query appears in
  output; the app never blocks waiting for them (no reply → defaults: cursor style 1,
  and the two DSR requests are simply never answered, with zero behavioral effect).
- Frame size depends on the terminal size at the moment of the frame
  (H = min(content, rows), W = min(content, cols) inline; full terminal in -f).

payload.resultSummary:
Area 8 is complete. Deliverable written to `/harness/notes/08-protocol.md` (317 lines), backed by ~40 capture scenarios in `/harness/captures/08/`, three test JSONs in `/harness/tests/08/`, and a new runner `/harness/pty3.py` (pty2.py + auto-replies to DECRQSS/DSR, `--decrqss-style N`, `SIGNAL:SIGxxx` tokens).

Key findings for the reimplementation:

- **Startup**: `\x00` + DECRQSS `\x1bP$q q\x1b\\` + (`\x1b[?1049h` iff `-f`) + `\x1b[?7l` + mouse-on ×4 (`1000,1003,1015,1006`) + `\x00`. stdin-pipe mode prepends `Reading from stdin...` (no newline). Fully deterministic — repeated runs byte-identical.
- **Frame grammar**: prefix (undo of previous frame's cursor move `\x1b[{U}B\x1b[{L}C`, `\r`, then `\x1b[1A`×(H_old−1) — singly, never combined), content rows joined by `\r\r\n`, suffix (`\x1b[{U}A\x1b[{L}D` to the selected cell, `\x1b[?25l`, `\x00`). Formulas: `U = H−1−sel_row`, `L = W+1−cursor_col` where cursor_col is the *last* column of the inverted token. Zero-valued moves are omitted; negative values are emitted literally — root scalar `42` produces the `\x1b[-1A` / `\x1b[-1B` quirk.
- **DSR `\x1b[6n`**: emitted in exactly the 2nd and 3rd frames of the session, positioned after the up-moves, before content — regardless of triggers and regardless of whether the terminal replies. DSR replies change nothing (verified byte-identical).
- **Clear mode**: `\x1b[2K` per line iff frame dims changed since last frame (resize OR expand/collapse); `\x1b[J\x1b[H` appended iff the frame got *narrower* (verified for both SIGWINCH- and content-driven changes).
- **Exit**: q/ESC (byte-identical) = one final full redraw + shutdown burst (undo, mouse-off in exact reverse order, `\x1b[?7h`, `\x1b[?1049l` iff `-f`, `\x1b[?25h`, `\x1b[{S} q`, then `\x00\r\r\n` inline / `\x00\r` fullscreen). **{S} echoes the DECRQSS reply** (default `1` on no/error reply — a harness-visible dependency). SIGINT/SIGTERM exit cleanly (code 0) with *no* redraw; SIGHUP kills with zero output; Ctrl-C/Ctrl-D *bytes* are just unknown keys.
- **Input**: one frame per read() batch — even no-ops and unknown keys redraw; `xx` in one write = 1 frame, two writes 10 ms apart = 2 frames. Lone-ESC timeout ≈ 80 ms. No idle/animation output.
- **NUL inventory**: exactly 4 positions (session start, after mouse-on, end of every frame, in the exit burst).
- **Cross-area flag**: the `-k` table claims `gg`=top / `G`=bottom, but observed behavior is **swapped** (`gg`→bottom, `G`→top, verified on two docs) — flagged in the notes for the keybindings agent.

## Key findings (all verified by PTY captures)

**Selection model prerequisite:** selection is a single *value cell* (`{`, `[`, `{...}`, `[...]`, or scalar token), not a row. It can point to a hidden node (inside a collapsed ancestor) — then no inverse is rendered, but `+`/`-` still act from that hidden node.

**`+` (deep expand) — one wavefront per press:**
1. V = selected node; if hidden, V = nearest visible ancestor-or-self; if scalar, V = parent container.
2. Expand ALL visible collapsed containers at the *minimum* depth in subtree(V) including V.
3. If none: complete no-op — `+` does **not** walk up beyond the parent (verified: 3 extra `+` presses with selection on scalar `f` change nothing even though collapsed `g` exists elsewhere).

**`-` (deep collapse) — one wavefront per press, asymmetric:**
1. C = selected node; while subtree(C)∪{C} has no visible expanded container, C = parent(C) (walk-up **does** continue, unlike `+`); no ancestors left → no-op.
2. Collapse ALL visible expanded containers at the *maximum* depth (e.g. `c` and `e` collapse together; both items of a table array collapse together).
3. `-` **never moves the selection** — collapsing an ancestor of the selection just hides the inverse highlight. It is not "collapse parent": with selection on collapsed `g`, `-` collapsed the deeper expanded sibling `a`.

**ENTER:** toggles the selected container one level (works on root → one-line `{...}`); no-op on scalars and on a root scalar. LEFT/RIGHT arrows are no-ops on value cells.

**Initial state:** root always expanded; depth-1 **objects** expanded, depth-1 **arrays** collapsed (even empty ones); depth ≥2 all collapsed. Object keys are displayed **sorted**. Expansion state is fully persistent per node across collapse/re-expand.

**Mouse:** click on a container value cell toggles it but does **not** move keyboard selection — and produces a double-inverse artifact (both keyboard-selected and clicked cells inverse, clicked-cell highlight persists across later frames). Click on a scalar moves selection there. Clicks on keys, the `(table view)` hint, or closing-brace rows are no-ops.

**Rendering bytes:** collapsed = `\x1b[1m{...},\x1b[22m` (comma inside bold, stays visible); when selected, inverse **replaces** bold: `\x1b[7m{...},\x1b[27m`. `(table view)` hint = 3 spaces + `\x1b[90m\x1b[49m(table view)\x1b[39m\x1b[49m`, shown iff array is non-empty and all elements are objects (mixed arrays don't qualify), on both collapsed and expanded header rows. Empty containers: no special `{}` — expanded = two rows, collapsed = `{...}`.

**Flags for other areas:** every input event (even no-ops/unknown keys) emits a full frame; two identical-state no-op frames differed in the leading cursor-dance up-count (19× vs 20× `\x1b[1A`) — possibly DSR-related, deferred to Area 03. Root-scalar frames emit literal `\x1b[-1A`/`\x1b[-1B`. `gg` moved selection to the *last* value row, not the top — flagged for the navigation agent.</subagent>
